audits.jarvis_gap: The trigger->spawn->act loop now has intent-aware fit, per-attempt provenance, breakers, quota folding and failover. Prior runs already proposed fixes for tiering, caching, resume, admission, coalescing, continuity and budget binding. Three blind spots are left. (1) Provider plan exhaustion. When a subscription CLI hits its usage limit, the error is recorded as a generic per-catalog-entry runtime_failure. Failover does not know which entries share that account, there is no notion of a reset time, and live owner turns keep paying to probe the exhausted account. (2) Turn order on one chat. Owner edits are dropped by idempotency dedup. Rapid follow-ups become independent concurrent sessions that can both act on the same instruction. (3) How hard the model thinks. That is baked into a catalog row's opaque extra_args rather than chosen per dispatch. Ideally the system knows how much provider allowance it has and when it returns. It treats the owner's correction as an amendment to the turn it corrects. And it buys deeper reasoning only where the stakes call for it. The owner can then stop wondering why a reply failed at 3pm, whether "actually make it 8" will create two reminders, and whether routine sweeps are paying for maximum reasoning effort.

audits.ideal: Every dispatch knows three things before it spends anything: which provider accounts have allowance and when exhausted ones come back, whether an earlier turn on the same chat is still in flight or has been amended by the owner, and how much reasoning the stakes warrant. Deterministic infrastructure enforces all three. Each choice is shown in the receipt, so the owner never has to reconcile duplicate actions or investigate opaque capacity failures.

audits.jarvis_gap: Prior runs have already proposed most attractive new external services: bank, flight, parcel, transit, weather/AQI, FHIR, telephony, notification mirror, Immich, Slack, GitHub, Readwise, Paperless, Todoist, Grocy, watched-source and others. RFC 0018 also says to harden existing senses before adding new ones (v1.md anti-patterns). The remaining gap is narrower. The fleet holds senses it does not use and lacks reference knowledge of the world. (1) Google Health already has the owner's activity_and_fitness and health_metrics_and_measurements consent, yet it polls only 7 daily/sleep rollups. Workouts are deferred by spec, so Chronicler's workout adapter has no producer. Exercise inference needs HR above 100 bpm, but the connector only supplies daily resting HR. Chronicler's own promise, "when did I last go running?", is therefore unanswerable from first-party sensors. (2) Every dwell cluster the owner has not declared is labelled place_unknown, because geocoding is excluded by spec. The fleet sees that the owner spent 2 hours somewhere but cannot say it was a hawker centre, a gym or a clinic. (3) The fleet has no civic calendar. Its seasonal presets are US-only (us-tax-season, US semesters) for an owner whose code defaults to Asia/Singapore. Routine-break flags and scheduling treat a lunar-dated public holiday as an ordinary weekday. Ideal: these three senses are deterministic, local or already consented, carry provenance and age, and never claim more than the evidence supports.

audits.jarvis_gap: Today the graph records which butler and session wrote an artifact, but not who wrote the words it was learned from. Any successful session's output becomes an episode. That includes sessions that only read a stranger's email or a passive group chat. Consolidation then mines those episodes for new rules (procedural guidance) and owner-anchored facts. Both are injected into every later session: Active Rules, Profile Facts, and the Fleet Knowledge section of every other butler's spawn context. So third-party text can become standing guidance across the fleet with no owner involvement. On the ask side, an honest 'I don't know' is a dead end. It is either a sourceless conversation_reply or an `unanswerable` dead letter, and the system forgets the owner ever asked. When the fact arrives a week later, the owner has to remember to ask again. On scale, every superseded or disowned memory leaves a stale row in the cross-butler catalog. That catalog has no GC owner, even though its grant model says GC is centralised. Ideal: guidance and self-model facts are born only from owner-authored or owner-endorsed evidence, with authority derived server-side and never read from prose. An unanswered owner question stays open and closes itself, with a citation, when the fact is written. The shared index stays bounded, so cross-butler recall does not slowly degrade into a false 'nothing relevant'.

audits.jarvis_gap: Today the fleet can store a decision or a research note but cannot think something through with the owner. Health 'research' is a stable fact keyed by title, holding one free-text URL. Web reach depends on whichever runtime binary is installed: the Claude adapter passes no tool restriction and records only tool_use inputs, not what came back. Finance only looks backward, apart from a linear forecast for the current month. Health only finds passive co-occurrences, which expire after seven days. Decision records and Commissions exist as proposals only; neither is built. The ideal: the owner commissions a question once. The owning specialist then works it over bounded sessions against hash-pinned source receipts and the owner's own data, and concludes honestly as answered, contested or insufficient evidence. Options are compared in cells that specialists compute, never in cells an LLM types. The assumptions behind a decision are watched in plain code, with no LLM, so a broken premise reaches the owner before the scheduled look-back. Personal trials ('does X help me?') close with an adherence-aware verdict from the owner's own measurements.

audits.jarvis_gap: Today the only ambient projection the fleet has shipped is the calendar subscribe feed (/api/calendar/subscribe.ics). The current OwnerAuthMiddleware almost certainly blocks native calendar apps from it: every /api/ path needs a passkey session cookie or the full-authority X-API-Key. When a calendar source fails, the feed silently returns a partial calendar. The deterministic attention verdict (briefing classify) can only be reached through the owner-only, LLM-elaborated briefing, which has no validity horizon. Telegram messages are edited only to resolve approvals. Voice is fenced to replies in the room the request came from. So no wall display, widget, watch face, e-ink panel, car or lock screen can show the one thing that matters, or show honestly that it has not been re-checked. The ideal is a projection layer. Each external surface gets a scoped, revocable read grant whose fetches are themselves watched. Every payload is deterministic, carries coverage, has a valid_until horizon so the edge can show 'unverified since' even when the host is dead, and is redacted to its audience. Dated obligations land in the owner's native calendar with alarms, a feed-incomplete sentinel replaces silent omission, and a single silent status line keeps calm visible without a ping.

audits.jarvis_gap: The fleet can ask (delegate_ask), announce (domain events) and gather evidence (fleet cases), but it has no sanctioned way for one specialist to request that another act. So every cross-domain action still goes through the owner by hand: Travel books a trip, and the owner has to tell Home himself. Meanwhile the ask channel already pastes the asker's free text verbatim into a prompt for a session that holds every write tool, so an "ask" can become an act that leaves no record. RFC 0032 explicitly dropped delegate_act and RFC 0026 never picked it up. Nothing in the code, the specs or the beads covers it.
audits.ideal: Any domain butler can file a typed mandate against an intent that a sibling has declared in git (for example home.away_window, requestable by travel). Switchboard checks the contract before routing it. The target receives only a mandate_id and reads the typed fields as reference data. Its own LLM session decides whether to accept or decline, and anything consequential goes through the target's own approval gate and RFC 0028 risk classes. The resulting pending action is stamped origin='mandated' with the mandate_id, so the owner's approval card reads "Travel asked Home: away window for trip X". The approval executor reports acted, failed, rejected or expired back to the mandate deterministically. The asker can withdraw a mandate (for example when the trip is cancelled), which cancels any pending approval. A valid_until sweep and an unreported sweep close mandates that would otherwise stay open forever. Every mandate row on the dashboard links to the asker session, the target session, the approval and the evidence. No authority ever moves between butlers.

moves.behavior_notes: Happy path: Travel books a trip and calls request_mandate('home.away_window', {trip_id, start, end}). Switchboard verifies the contract and routes it. Home's session accepts and calls the gated arm/scene tools. A pending action is created with origin='mandated', status moves to awaiting_owner, the owner approves, the executor runs, and the mandate becomes acted with evidence. Failure paths: an undeclared intent or a non-permitted requester is refused before any row is written; a route failure becomes unroutable or failed with a reason; an execution error becomes failed; a rejected or expired approval becomes declined or expired, with the decision recorded as evidence. Concurrency: a withdraw racing an owner approval is serialized by the executor action lock plus a CAS on pending_actions.status, and the loser records withdrawn_too_late with the actual outcome. Idempotence: re-sending the same (requester, idempotency_key) returns the existing mandate; a duplicate mandate_receive returns already_<status>; the terminal outcome is written once, through the partial unique index. Rollback: dropping the mandates core group returns the fleet to ask-only, and existing rows stay readable and inert. Withdrawal after an act schedules the target to consider a reversal and never undoes anything automatically. A valid_until sweep marks expired; a window-close sweep writes only unreported and never invents acted.

audits.jarvis_gap: The instance runs on the owner's own machines and tailnet (vision.md:11-13). Several senses already depend on tailnet hosts: ActivityWatch reaches its machine over MagicDNS (activitywatch.py:63-65), and beads/Dolt live on a ts.net host. Yet no connector perceives those machines. A node key expiring, a host leaving the tailnet or a self-hosted service going down shows up only later as a silent or degraded sense, with no root cause attached. The lifecycle engine to hold these concerns honestly already exists (owner_conditions.py:116-152, a snapshot-authoritative ledger with a locked reconcile). The missing pieces are the sense and an owner for the domain.
audits.ideal: A read-only homelab connector polls the Tailscale device API and a declared list of service, TCP and TLS endpoints. It writes complete-or-incomplete snapshots to connectors.homelab_observations. A job-only Steward butler turns each snapshot into owner conditions with lead time: a node key that will expire, a critical node offline, a service down, a TLS certificate close to expiry. A stale or failed snapshot never resolves a condition, and the page says "tailnet view stale since T" rather than "all healthy". Each silent connector gets an upstream-host clause, for example "ActivityWatch: host 'desktop' last seen on the tailnet 9 days ago, key expired". The owner can ask the Steward "are my machines ok?" through Switchboard and get an answer backed by evidence, and the existing Standing Conditions tile shows the open episodes with deadlines.

moves.behavior_notes:
Happy path: the AW host's key expires in 10 days, so a complete snapshot opens steward:node-key-expiring with the deadline in its metadata and the owner gets one insight. After re-auth the next complete snapshot omits the node and the condition resolves as 'satisfied'.
Failure: a Tailscale 401 or 5xx writes snapshot_complete=false plus the error. The heartbeat goes degraded with a reason. Steward reconciles with snapshot_complete=False, so nothing resolves, and the page says 'tailnet view stale since T', never green.
Concurrency: overlapping reconcile runs serialize on the condition_ledger advisory lock per source (condition_ledger.py:477).
Idempotence: the unique (snapshot_id, asset_key) constraint makes re-ingesting a snapshot a no-op. Fingerprints use the nodeId, not the hostname, so a rename does not churn episodes.
Rollback: disabling the connector freezes conditions as stale rather than resolving them. Removing Steward resolves its sources with reason 'cancelled' via resolve_condition. The core table is additive.
Attribution: attribution reports host state only when the dependency is declared, and never guesses it from URL strings.

audits.jarvis_gap: The fleet has dense personal time series (wearable vitals, energy, spend, time lanes) but no honest way to say "this is unusual for you". Five butlers each improvise their own idea of "usual". None of them reports how much data it rests on or whether the sensor behind it is alive. Home's "baseline" is just last week's number, stored as prose and parsed back with a regex. Health only scans weekly. So the most JARVIS-like unprompted sentence, "your resting heart rate has been above your normal for 3 days", cannot be said, and the comparisons that do exist present weak or stale numbers as an established norm.
audits.ideal: Every butler that owns a numeric series declares it once as a BaselineMetric. A deterministic daily job in that butler's own schema computes a robust personal band: median plus or minus k times MAD (median absolute deviation), bucketed by day, day of week or week. Each band records how many observations it saw against how many it expected, plus coverage, and is gated by the expected_signals measurability check. Days inside an open deviation episode are left out of the window, so an illness week never becomes the new normal. One core scorer is the only sanctioned way to claim a deviation. It returns one of within, above, below, insufficient_history, stale or unmeasurable, and never claims "normal" from a dead instrument. A run of k days outside the band opens a deviation episode. The episode proposes one insight carrying its sample size and a door to a chart with the band drawn, and it is reconciled as an owner condition that closes silently when the value returns. Sessions get a core MCP tool so the LLM can only say "unusual for you" by citing a computed band. The five ad-hoc baselines are retired.

moves.integration_points: CORE: src/butlers/core/baselines.py, pure and deterministic. Provides BaselineMetric (key, unit, bucket day|dow|week, window_days, min_n, min_coverage, k_mad, k_consecutive, concern above|below|both, min_dispersion, expected_signal_key) plus compute_baseline(samples, expected_count), score(value, baseline, now) -> Deviation{state, mad_units, n_observed, n_expected, coverage} and persist/episode helpers. MIGRATION: alembic/versions/core/core_255_metric_baselines.py, unqualified so it fans out per butler schema with DML grants, mirroring core_220. Adds metric_baselines (PK metric_key, bucket_value, method_version; center, dispersion, n_observed, n_expected, coverage, unit, measurability, input_digest, computed_at) and metric_deviation_episodes (id, metric_key, opened_on, closed_on, direction, peak_mad, status open|closed, UNIQUE(metric_key, opened_on)). Health metrics live in roster/health/jobs/baselines.py, replacing _scan_measurement_drift_correlation (health_jobs.py:875-965); home replaces energy_baseline prose facts (home.py:1551-1574, 1940-1985); finance moves compute_baselines storage off spending_baseline facts (anomaly_detection.py:121-298), retires the briefing's 2x average (briefing.py:437-460), and uses currency-scoped metric keys. It also reconciles an owner condition via reconcile_owner_condition (roster/switchboard/modules/owner_conditions_broker.py:100) and resolves it on close. MCP: core tool group src/butlers/core_tools/_baselines.py exposing metric_baseline_get(metric_key) -> {state, band, n, coverage, computed_at, stale}, read-only over the caller's own schema. API: GET /api/health/baselines and /api/home/baselines in roster/{butler}/api/router.py, using the degraded envelope from docs/api_and_protocols/response-conventions.md. UI: ButlerHealthMeasurementsTab draws the band with an 'n of m days' plaque; an insufficient or unmeasurable band renders as words, not a band. SPECS: new openspec/specs/personal-baselines/spec.md; amend proactive-insight-engine (any deviation-claiming category must carry baseline_evidence), finance-anomaly-detection (storage and method), owner-condition-ledger (deviation source naming). TRUST: each butler reads only its own schema; the Switchboard is reached only through the existing broker and conditions MCP/direct-import path; the daemon job is pure statistics with no LLM; this is core rather than a module because the table and scheduler-run job are core infrastructure.
moves.behavior_notes: Happy: 60 days of resting_hr with 54 observed and a healthy connector gives band 52-58. Three consecutive days at 2.6 MAD or more above it open one episode and one candidate. A return to the band closes the episode and resolves the condition with no message. Failure (instrument): expected signal UNMEASURABLE gives a measurability row of 'unmeasurable'; score returns unmeasurable; no candidate; the blind-spot preamble already names the gap. Failure (thin data): coverage below min_coverage or n below min_n gives insufficient_history, never 'within'. Stale: a band older than 2x the refresh interval scores as stale and suppresses candidates. Contamination: days inside an open episode are excluded from the window, so the band does not chase the anomaly. MAD=0: dispersion is floored at the declared min_dispersion. Concurrency: a per-metric pg_advisory_xact_lock plus UNIQUE(metric_key, opened_on) means a catch-up run and the scheduled run cannot open two episodes. Idempotence: an unchanged input_digest makes the upsert a no-op, and a same-day rerun hits the broker's dedup_key. Rollback: method_version lets a v2 run alongside v1 in shadow; disabling the baseline_watch schedule silences the producer; downgrade drops both per-schema tables (backward compat waived).

audits.jarvis_gap: The token system is mature for contrast against backgrounds, but the five-second scan rests on two things it never checks. First, state marks carry state through hue alone: light-theme degraded and error dots fall below a just-noticeable difference under deuteranopia, and forced-colors mode erases them entirely. Second, trend charts draw irregular readings as evenly spaced smooth curves that end at the last reading rather than at now, so the geometry makes up both cadence and currency.
audits.ideal: Every state the owner scans is told apart by shape as well as hue, so it survives any eye, any theme, forced-colors, grayscale and print. A computed CVD-separation gate makes it impossible to ship a palette where error looks like degraded, or where a chart series wears the state amber. Every trend chart is time-true. Its x-axis spans the requested window and ends at now, each real observation is a visible mark, joins between readings are never smoothed, and a long silence breaks the line. Absence and staleness are therefore visible in the geometry rather than only in a caption. A lint rule and a shared primitive enforce one grammar across all surfaces, so these rules do not depend on each page's discipline.

design_addenda.title: Steward: perceive the owner's tailnet machines and self-hosted services, hold equipment conditions with lead time, and attribute silent senses to their upstream host
design_addenda.why: vision.md:11-13 (you own the instance, on your own infrastructure) and vision.md:135 (success is mental labor absorbed). Today the owner has to watch Tailscale key expiry, host liveness and self-hosted service uptime himself, and he finds out only after a sense has gone quiet. The payoff is a deadline-bearing warning before a key expires and a named root cause when one fails. Stale data can never pass for 'all healthy'.
design_addenda.integration_points:
CONNECTOR: new src/butlers/connectors/homelab.py, following connector-base-spec obligations (heartbeat connector_type='homelab' via heartbeat.py:131, cursor_store checkpoint of the last snapshot, metrics, health port, source filters). Two probe families. (a) Tailscale device API, read-only OAuth client, keyed on the stable nodeId with lastSeen, expires, keyExpiryDisabled and updateAvailable. (b) Declared HTTP/TCP/TLS-notAfter probes from HOMELAB_TARGETS JSON config, in the LIVE_LISTENER_DEVICES style; it never scans the network. Credential stored as RFC 0004 entity_info.type 'tailscale_oauth_client' via core credentials.
TABLES: core migration alembic/versions/core/core_2xx_homelab_observations.py creates connectors.homelab_observations (snapshot_id, asset_key, kind, observed_at, state jsonb, snapshot_complete bool, error text; unique snapshot_id+asset_key). INSERT for connector_writer, SELECT for butler_steward_rw, modelled on core_084. Butler schema 'steward' (roster/steward/migrations/001): steward.assets (asset_key, display_name, criticality fleet_dependency|owner_service|incidental) and steward.asset_dependencies (asset_key, dependent_endpoint_identity, e.g. 'activitywatch:desktop').
BUTLER: roster/steward/{MANIFESTO.md, butler.toml (schema steward, dispatch_mode="job" schedule 'equipment-reconcile' every 15 min), jobs/steward_jobs.py, api/router.py, api/models.py}. The job calls owner_conditions.reconcile_snapshot with sources steward:node-key-expiring, steward:node-offline, steward:service-down and steward:tls-expiring, and delivers through propose_insight_candidate or notify(priority='high' only for fleet_dependency nodes going offline; _notifications.py:290-298).
MCP TOOLS (Steward module, read and annotate only): steward_assets_list(filter) returns assets with last observation and open condition ids. steward_asset_status(asset_key) returns an observation history window. steward_asset_annotate(asset_key, criticality, depends_on[]) refuses unknown asset_keys. There are no actuation tools.
API: GET /api/steward/assets (cursor pagination, degraded envelope when the homelab heartbeat is older than 3x its interval), GET /api/steward/assets/{key}, GET /api/steward/attribution?endpoint_identity=. Dashboard: a /steward page; an 'Upstream host' clause on the connector detail page; the existing StandingConditionsTile (frontend/src/components/system/StandingConditionsTile.tsx) shows the steward:* sources.
SPECS: new openspec/specs/connector-homelab and butler-steward; amend the owner-condition-ledger source registry, RFC 0004 (credential type) and RFC 0006 (connectors.homelab_observations). Add RFC 0003 channel/provider 'homelab/tailscale' only when transition ingest lands.
DEPLOY: deploy/helm/butlers/values.yaml connectors list (lines 163-256) gets homelab; networkpolicy egress allows api.tailscale.com plus the declared targets.
TRUST: the connector holds the only credential and never actuates. The Steward daemon is deterministic and never reads Tailscale directly. LLM access goes only through Steward MCP tools via Switchboard routing. Connector config is the inventory, so the connector never reads the steward schema.

S1 (independently shippable): homelab connector polling the Tailscale inventory only, the core_2xx table plus grants, helm values, and a job-only Steward skeleton (manifesto, toml, migrations) reconciling node-key-expiring and node-offline. S2: declared HTTP/TCP/TLS-expiry probes plus steward:service-down and steward:tls-expiring.
S3: steward.asset_dependencies, steward_asset_annotate, the attribution route and the 'Upstream host' clause on the connector detail page.

design_addenda.title: Research briefs: a commissioned, resumable inquiry with a claim ledger and an honest conclusion
design_addenda.why: Vision: the success measure is mental labor absorbed. 'Look into X and tell me by Friday' is labor the owner currently carries in their head across chat turns. 'Failure never impersonates health' means a brief must be able to conclude 'insufficient evidence' or 'contested' instead of a confident paragraph. Payoff: the owner commissions once, can stop tracking it, and gets a durable object whose every claim opens a receipt or an owner-data record, plus an as-of and a refresh date.
design_addenda.integration_points: Migration public.research_briefs (id, owning_butler, question, owner_constraints jsonb, due_at, status commissioned|in_progress|answered|contested|insufficient_evidence|withdrawn, conclusion, refresh_after, session_budget, sessions_used), public.research_brief_claims (brief_id, claim, stance supports|contradicts|qualifies, load_bearing bool, receipt_ids uuid[], owner_data_refs jsonb in the citations.py internal grammar, credence class), public.research_brief_gaps; core tools brief_commission/brief_add_claim/brief_add_gap/brief_conclude in src/butlers/core_tools/_briefs.py; follow-up sessions via schedule_create one-shot (core_tools/_scheduling.py:68) + continuity ledger (_continuity.py); cross-domain evidence via existing delegation (_delegation.py) recorded as owner_data claims; GET /api/briefs, /api/briefs/{id}; dashboard /briefs list + detail registered in shell-capability.ts; new openspec/specs/research-briefs/spec.md.
